### Observed differences

- Before, A19, A20 and A25 each led almost exclusively to A26 (about 92, 94 and 99 in 100 of their observed outgoing transitions); in the later window they lead mainly to A32 (about 45–56 in 100) and A28 (about 39–48 in 100), with A26 as their successor almost unobserved (0–2 in 100). [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003]
- A45 changed target: before it led to A25, A19 and A20 (about 35, 35 and 24 in 100), with A45 immediately followed by A25 in about 93 in 100 of observed pairs; in the later window it leads to A26 in about 94 in 100, typically immediately, while A45 followed by A25 within five steps nearly disappears (1 observed pair). [DIR006, LAG010, LAG011]
- The chain A27 → A28 → A32 loosened: before, A27 led to A28 in about 98 in 100 and A28 to A32 in about 99 in 100; in the later window A27 leads to A28 in about 54 in 100 and to A19, A20 or A25 in about 42 in 100 combined, and A28 leads to A32 in about 45 in 100 and back to A20, A25 or A19 in about 21, 17 and 16 in 100, the step back typically being immediate (A28 followed by A19 or A20 at the next position in about 92 and 98 in 100 of observed pairs). A27 and A32 are now typically three positions apart instead of two. [DIR004, DIR005, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]
- Event positions shifted accordingly: the median position of A19, A20 and A25 moved from about 0.29–0.31 to about 0.60–0.62 of the trace, A26 moved slightly earlier (median about 0.34 to 0.31) and A27 stayed at about 0.56–0.59; A26 and A27 occur in every trace in both windows, and A19, A20 and A25 each appear in a similar share of traces in both windows (about 25–39 in 100 before, 30–38 after). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]
- Pairwise order reversed: before, A19, A20 and A25 each ran before A26 and before A27 in roughly 24–38 in 100 of the traces containing both; in the later window A26 and A27 each run before them in about 28–37 in 100. A20 and A25 now appear both before and after A28, so their order relative to A28 is mixed. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- A24 was observed in about 43 in 100 traces before and about 58 in 100 after (mean occurrences per trace 0.43 vs 0.58). [OCC001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the activities A19, A20 and A25 changed their placement in the sequence. In the earlier window they ran together early in the case, before A26 and A27, fed by A45, while A27 → A28 → A32 formed a separate later chain; in the later window A26 has taken the early slot and is reached directly from A45, and A19, A20 and A25 now run late, entered after A27, from where they lead to A28 and A32, with A28 stepping back to the group before A32 is reached. This rests on direct relational and positional evidence: the successor profiles of A19, A20, A25, A27, A28 and A45 changed wholesale, every measured pair between the group and A26 or A27 reversed its usual order, and the group's median position moved from about three-tenths to about three-fifths through the trace while its participation stayed similar — fitting a move of existing, optional activities rather than activities appearing or disappearing. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011]

Chance is an unlikely explanation for the evidence as a whole: 31 items qualified across 124 tested units where about 0.62 would be expected without a change, and every item's difference exceeds about 995 in 1000 random re-splits. Limitations: positions and lags are measured in event positions, not clock time, so the change is one of sequence placement; a few lag comparisons rest on very few observations (for example A19 followed by A26 has 2, and A45 followed by A25 has 1, observed pairs in the later window) and were not needed for the hypothesis. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that only part of the cases adopted the new arrangement, since each window aggregates 200 traces; it also cannot show whether the step from A28 back to the group is a repetition of the same activities within a case. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG007, LAG008, LAG010, REL005, REL008]

Other differences: A24's participation rose from about 43 to about 58 in 100 traces; the evidence contains no relational or positional items for A24, so it cannot be tied to the reordering described above. [OCC001]
